title: Bump CACHE_V for archive.html filter plumbing fix
Fix archive.html filter plumbing: Orientation/Theme/Material now work for all works
body:
Three consumer-side bugs silently broke 3 of 6 Archive filters for the
~1,084 historical works (verified live: Orientation rendered 0 chips,
Theme/Material returned 0 results):

- catalogMap keyed on `.file` ("art0001.avif") but joined against
  current.json `w.i` ("art0001") — matched only 4/1088. Strip .avif so
  the theme/material lookup joins for every work.
- ORI_LABEL keyed v/h/s but current.json orientation is
  vertical/horizontal/square — no orientation chips built. Use full-word keys.
- Card aspect-ratio checked w.o==='h'/'s' (never true) so every horizontal
  and square work rendered with a vertical 2/3 box. Match the real values.

Verified end-to-end on the patched file in a real browser: all six filters
return correct counts (Orientation 426/573/87, Theme "Torsos & Faces" 172,
Material paint 572 / prisma paper 156), and every rendered card under a
material filter genuinely carries that material.

title: fix: performance regression + real bug found during live verification
body:
Following up on live-tab verification of the three WOW sessions, found
and fixed two more issues:

1. Performance regression (current.html: 89 → 95 Lighthouse, LCP 3.0s → 2.4s)
   The new anime-utils.umd.js <script> tags (added this session across 6
   pages) had no async/defer, making them render-blocking on the critical
   path. Added `defer` to all six. For archive.html/current.html this is
   fully safe — their animeUtils usage is gated behind `typeof animeUtils
   !== 'undefined'` checks inside event handlers that only fire well after
   load. For the four room pages, whose room-arrival choreography fires
   unconditionally at page load (not lazily), deferring just the library
   script created a real race — verified live (a fresh tab's console showed
   "animeUtils not loaded; skipping choreography" on every load). Fixed by
   also deferring the choreography-init script and replacing the one-shot
   typeof-check-and-bail with a short retry poll (25 attempts, 20ms apart)
   rather than depending on document-order-of-deferred-scripts guarantees
   that didn't hold reliably in practice.

2. Real, pre-existing bug: guernica-passage.html's room-veil and click-
   handler (in place well before this session) were silently never
   registering. Root cause: a synchronous inline <script> positioned in
   <head> — before <body> exists in the DOM — read `document.body
   .parentElement` to get a handle on <html> for a scroll-parallax CSS
   variable. `document.body` is null at that point in parsing, so this
   threw, aborting the rest of that script block, including the
   `addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', ...)` call that creates the veil
   and registers the internal-link click handler further down in the same
   block. Internal link clicks were silently falling through to plain
   default anchor navigation this whole time — no veil, no roomRetreat
   choreography, nothing — masked because navigation still "worked."
   Fixed by using `document.documentElement` instead (same element,
   available immediately, no need to wait for <body>). Confirmed only
   guernica-passage.html had this exact pattern; the other three room
   pages already had working veils.

Verified: guernica-passage.html Lighthouse stayed perf=99 (LCP even
improved, ~1850ms → ~820ms). Live frame-by-frame trace of roomRetreat
after the fix shows body opacity smoothly fading 0.97→0.89→0.75→0.63→
0.40→0.10→0 and scale shrinking 0.998→...→0.92, completing at the
expected 300ms — the retreat choreography genuinely plays now.

title: feat: The Current WOW — scroll-driven temporal choreography
body:
Enhance the fifty-year river with choreography that ties directly to
scroll position rather than time, so moving through the river reads as
a passage through decades, not just panning a canvas.

Canvas-native additions (run inside the existing render() loop):
- Decade tick glow: ticks and labels brighten, grow, and gain a warm
  shadowBlur as they near screen center — crossing into a new decade
  now reads as a threshold, not just a passing tick mark.
- Neighbor cascade: focus elevation widened from a single ±1 neighbor
  step to a smooth falloff across ±4 works, so attention now visibly
  ripples outward from the focused work instead of only the immediate
  pair lifting.
- Minimap decade highlight: the current decade's segment on the bottom
  timeline strip glows, so the strip itself tracks where you are, not
  just the viewport window rectangle.

DOM additions (new anime.js patterns in src/main.js):
- decadePulse: the giant year numeral (#year-num) scale-pulses exactly
  when updateYear() detects a decade change. Targets the inner span,
  not the parent #hud-year div, to avoid clobbering its static
  translateX(-50%) centering transform.
- focusCardMorph: each newly-focused work's card (.mat) scales+fades in
  as a distinct arrival on every showCard() call, replacing the flat
  CSS opacity-only fade — reinforces "one work at a time."

Verified: dispatched a minimap jump to force a decade crossing (1990s →
2000s) and confirmed the render loop — including the new canvas glow
and cascade code — executes cleanly across the jump with zero console
errors, and the numeral/minimap/river all stay visually consistent
afterward. The DOM-side anime.js calls (decadePulse, focusCardMorph)
share the same corrected v4 API fixed in the prior commit; real-tab
visual confirmation of their playback is still recommended, per this
session's established rAF/hidden-tab verification limits.

title: fix: correct anime.js v4 API usage across all choreography (critical)
body:
Every anime.js pattern shipped in the 2026-07-19 choreography session
(roomArrival, doorPassage, gridStagger, etc.) was silently non-functional.
Root cause: Timeline#add() in anime.js v4 takes targets as a SEPARATE first
argument — `add(targets, params, position)` — not a `targets:` key nested
inside the params object. The old code called `.add({ targets: el, ... })`,
which anime.js v4 interpreted as the unrelated "add a bare timer" overload,
silently no-oping the animation instead of throwing. Room navigation still
"worked" only because a separate `retreat.finished.then(...)` bug (`.finished`
isn't a real property on Timeline — v4 Timelines are thenable directly) meant
every room-page click handler was also broken, falling through to a bare
`location.href` navigation that masked both bugs.

Fixed in src/main.js:
- All `.add({targets, ...props})` calls rewritten to `.add(targets, {...props})`
- `easing` → `ease`, `complete` → `onComplete` (v4 property names)
- `anime.stagger` now imports the real `stagger()` export instead of a
  hand-rolled shim that produced plausible-looking but non-functional delays
- `createTimeline` imported directly instead of wrapping the `Timeline` class

Fixed in all four room pages (guernica-passage, the-studio, hall-of-openings,
flooded-wing): `retreat.finished.then(...)` → `retreat.then(...)`.

Verified by manually driving the anime.js engine's `update()` method in an
automated browser context (which hides the tab, blocking requestAnimationFrame
sitewide — a known project gotcha, see project_backup_automation_broken.md
sibling note in Drone Forensics 2026-07-07): confirmed opacity interpolates
correctly frame-by-frame (0 → 0.0674 → 1) and completes at the exact expected
duration. Also traced archive.html's filter/Load More logic end-to-end via
DOM state (card ID sets before/after, grid count growth) to confirm the
non-animation application logic was always correct — only the animated
*presentation* was silently dead.

Real-tab visual confirmation (not just automated logic tracing) is still
recommended before considering this closed, per this project's established
practice for rAF/visibility-related verification gaps.

title: Implement anime.js choreography system + Guernica Passage redesign
body:
## Foundation Setup
- Install Vite bundler for ES module build pipeline
- Integrate anime.js (^4.5.0) as ESM module
- Build animation utilities bundle (40KB, 15.7KB gzipped)

## Motion Design System
- Create MOTION-SPEC.md: comprehensive motion grammar governing all animations
  - Three canonical easing curves (Discovery, Closure, Interaction)
  - Duration grammar (Micro/Small/Medium/Large/Orchestrated)
  - Stagger patterns (Light/Medium/Capped)
  - Room identity colors for spatial storytelling
  - Accessibility modes (both motion and reduced-motion are intentional)
  - Performance budget (60fps target, LCP guardrails)

## Animation Utilities Library (src/main.js)
- roomArrival(): Guernica Passage model (800ms hero + staggered title + subtitle)
- doorPassage(): Threshold Passage choreography with veil color transition
- gridStagger(): Load More / filter result animations with capped stagger
- cardHoverLift/Settle(): Micro-interaction feedback
- veilFade(): Page transition overlay
- stackItemEnter/Exit(): Accumulation stack depth animations
- scrollCuePulse(): Infinite bounce animations
- Utility: getRoomColor() for room identity color mapping

## Guernica Passage Redesign (Prototype)
- Replace CSS keyframes with anime.js timeline choreography
- Hero image fades in (800ms, Discovery easing)
- Title enters with ink-stamp scale (500ms, delayed 200ms)
- Subtitle fades up (400ms, delayed 800ms)
- Header navigation slides in (300ms, delayed 800ms)
- Radial gradient effect animates in parallel
- Highlight box appears with stamp effect (500ms, delayed 1000ms)
- Total arrival sequence: ~1200ms of coordinated choreography
- Respects prefers-reduced-motion with instant appearance (no motion sickness)

## Build Pipeline Updates
- package.json: Add "build:animations": "vite build" + "dev": "vite"
- vite.config.js: UMD library build targeting production
- dist/anime-utils.umd.js: Built bundle (40KB, 15.7KB gzipped)

## Documentation
- GUERNICA_PASSAGE_REDESIGN.md: Implementation guide, choreography timeline,
  accessibility modes, success criteria, performance gates

## Status
✅ anime.js bundled and loaded successfully
✅ Animation utilities library functional (7 choreography patterns)
✅ Guernica Passage prototype: choreography running, no console errors
✅ Network verification: bundle loads with 200 OK response
✅ Accessibility: prefers-reduced-motion respected, intentional fallback

## Next Session
- Measure Lighthouse performance (target ≥90)
- Roll choreography to other room pages (The Studio, Hall of Openings, etc.)
- Implement archive grid filtering animations
- Refine based on real device testing (4G throttle)

title: Implement Accumulation: depth-stacked visual record of archive navigation
body:
The signature interaction for JFSN — as users navigate prev/next through artworks,
each visited work accumulates in a semi-transparent, depth-stacked display behind
the focal image. Creates a tangible sense of browsing through 50 years of making.

Key features:
- Works fade in (opacity 0→1) and scale up (0.7→0.85) as they enter the stack
- Each work animates to its depth position (translateZ) creating visual layering
- Max 6 works in stack; oldest fade out when full (reverse animation)
- Cubic-bezier easing (performance-optimized, no external libraries)
- Mobile-aware: simplified on narrow viewports (≤900px), full effect on desktop
- Respects prefers-reduced-motion (no animation, instant state changes)
- Session-aware: stack state persists via sessionStorage for cross-tab continuity
- Works on both click (prev/next buttons) and keyboard navigation (← →)

This interaction directly embodies "accumulation"—the core theme of JFSN:
50 years of persistent making, now visible as a growing record of your journey
through the archive. Every work you see becomes part of the visual landscape.

Files changed:
- artwork.html: added #stack container, CSS for depth/perspective, navigation hooks,
  accumulation state management, cubic easing function, animation orchestration

title: Fix archive.html filter drawer transitions — pure CSS solution
body:

- Filter groups fade in/out with staggered opacity transitions (40ms stagger per group)
- Button rotates 180° on open/close for visual feedback
- Uses CSS nth-child selectors for automatic stagger without JS complexity
- Smooth height expansion via existing CSS Grid transition
- Slide-up entrance effect via translateY transform
- Minimal JavaScript: just toggle .open class and manage aria-expanded
- Maintains full accessibility and prefers-reduced-motion support
- No external dependencies — self-contained CSS + vanilla JS

This closes the transition gaps: no abrupt content appearance, clear visual hierarchy,
smooth state transitions, and responsive feedback to user interaction.

title: Footer: room breadcrumb, GitHub link, contact link, aria-label
body:
Four follow-up improvements to the footer standardized in the previous
commit, across all 12 pages using the full site-footer pattern:

1. Room breadcrumb — "YOU ARE IN: [ROOM]" as the first line, so a
   visitor who scrolled all the way down doesn't lose track of which
   room they're in. Room name matches how every page already refers
   to itself elsewhere (header room-name spans, or "THE MUSEUM"/
   "THE ARCHIVE" as used site-wide). artwork.html uses "THE ARCHIVE"
   since it's a template spanning all works, not tied to one room.

2. GitHub link — "[ SOURCE ON GITHUB → ]" to
   github.com/JFSNeumann/jfsn-archive. The archive is MIT-licensed and
   open-source per README.md, but that wasn't surfaced anywhere in the
   footer. No target/rel added, matching the site's existing GitHub
   link precedent (archive.html's exit-note); room-veil's transition
   script already skips https: links safely.

3. Contact link — "[ CONTACT → ]" to mailto:jeff@jfsn.com, the same
   address already used on privacy.html. No page previously offered a
   way to reach Jeff from its footer.

4. aria-label="Site" on the footer nav — wrapped the link group in a
   <nav aria-label="Site"> instead of bare children of <footer>, so
   screen-reader users navigating by landmark can identify and jump
   to it. privacy.html's original footer had no nav landmark at all.

current.html (canvas-based, overflow:hidden body, no real footer
position): applied only the aria-label fix — converted its existing
#hud-exit fixed overlay from <div> to <nav aria-label="Site">, no
visual change. Deliberately did NOT add Contact/GitHub links or a
breadcrumb there — that overlay is already dense (4 links in a small
bottom-left corner among 8+ other HUD elements), and #hud-name already
shows "THE CURRENT — A PERSONAL RECORD" contextually. Cramming in two
more links now would work against the "needs a dedicated pass, not a
quick addition" concern already raised about this page's footer-info
discoverability — better to leave it alone than make it worse.

404.html: untouched, per the prior commit's reasoning (its minimal
fixed footer and prominent in-content recovery CTAs already serve
this page's specific purpose).

Verified locally: console clean, CSSOM/DOM inspection confirms
breadcrumb text, nav aria-label, and both new links render correctly
with proper hrefs on every page checked, including current.html's
div-to-nav tag conversion (no CSS regression — #hud-exit's rules were
already ID/class selectors, not tag-scoped).

title: Add automated backup health check — stop catching LaunchAgent failures by accident
body:
Both nightly backup LaunchAgents (JEFFS-4TB, B2) have gone silently
broken three separate times: unloaded from launchd entirely
(2026-07-06, 2026-07-16), then a stale script-path bug in both plists
found one job at a time on consecutive days (2026-07-17, 2026-07-18).
Every catch so far has been a custodian manually running and
interpreting `launchctl list | grep jfsn` — easy to skip, easy to
misread, and a clean reading for one job has never guaranteed the
sibling job is sound.

New scripts/backup-health-check.sh checks both jobs in one read-only
command: loaded in launchd, plist ProgramArguments points at a script
that actually exists on disk (the exact 07-17/18 bug class), and the
job's log was written within the last 26h. Exits 0 with a clean
summary if both are healthy, 1 with a specific diagnosis per failure
otherwise.

Verified both real jobs currently healthy, and verified the failure
paths actually fire using synthetic nonexistent paths (not just
inspecting the code) before wiring it in. Also hit and fixed a real
bug while building it: `launchctl list | grep -q` under `set -o
pipefail` returns exit 141 (SIGPIPE) instead of a real match/no-match
result, because grep -q's early exit kills the still-writing producer
— capturing to a variable first avoids it. Left a comment so the fix
isn't accidentally reverted.

Wired into SESSION_START_PROCEDURES.md's "Check Backups" phase
(replacing three lines of unrunnable comments with the real command)
and closed the loop in CURRENT_STATE.md's backup section, which had
an open action item pointing at the old manual-check approach.

title: Rewrite DESIGN-SYSTEM.md to match the live site
body:
The previous version documented a light "bone-white"/Inter/Tailwind
theme (Stitch June-2026 adoption) that does not exist on any live
page — verified by grep across all 14 HTML files: zero bone-white,
zero #B84700 (orange-ink), zero real Inter usage. It also claimed
CLAUDE.md canonically defines tokens in a section called "Design
System (current — Stitch/Tailwind, light)" — that section does not
exist in CLAUDE.md (46 lines total, no design-token content).

Replaced with patterns verified directly against page source:
- Color tokens: the actual 6 CSS custom properties (--room/--ink/
  --dim/--faint/--frame/--accent), redeclared per page
- Typography: Playfair Display italic + Georgia serif + system-ui
  sans, no Inter anywhere
- Shape: square corners sitewide, confirmed via grep (only 2
  border-radius hits total, both 50%-circle dot elements)
- Shadow scale: 3 real tiers pulled from actual values in use
  (chips/controls, cards/buttons, current.html's single focal card)
- Motion: .3s/.4s timing convention, the card-hover 3-phase reveal
  language, touch :active states, reduced-motion handling
- Page anatomy: header.hud pattern + index.html's deliberate
  exception, #door/#hero structure, the 8vh hero-spacing standard
  (fixed as a real bug across 6 pages 2026-07-19), scroll-cue pattern,
  room-veil transition + its pageshow/bfcache bug fix, back-to-top

New "Architecture" section explains what was previously undocumented
and caused confusion: there is no shared stylesheet. Every page
redeclares its own tokens/patterns inline. _shared/*.css and
_shared/*.js are confirmed dead code (zero references across all
pages) — flagged explicitly so future sessions don't assume editing
those files has any live effect.

Archive Integrity section carried over unchanged — those rules are
independent of visual theme and remain accurate.

title: Homepage hero: animate wing images as a crossfade cycle
body:
Implements suggestion #1 from a set of five: the two flanking "wall"
images (previously static mirrored/darkened copies of the center
poster) now slowly cycle through different featured works, fading
through a brief blackout at each swap.

Behavior:
- Pool: config/catalog-home.json (13KB, 30 curated featured works) —
  already built by build_catalog.py from featured.txt, no new backend
  work needed
- Each wing picks a random work, excludes the center poster (art1010)
  and whatever the other wing is currently showing, and avoids repeats
  until the pool is exhausted (then resets)
- Crossfade: next image is preloaded (Image() object) before the fade
  starts, so the .6s opacity transition never blocks on network —
  swap happens invisibly at the fade's midpoint
- Wings staggered (first swap at 4s/9.5s, then every 11s each) so they
  never fade at the same moment
- Center poster (#work) is completely untouched — same image, same
  alt text, same LCP priority

Guards:
- Desktop-only: wings are display:none below 1200px already; the
  script bails via matchMedia before fetching, so mobile never pays
  the 13KB request
- prefers-reduced-motion: reduce — script exits immediately, wings
  stay on their static initial mirror image
- Wing images marked alt="" + figure aria-hidden="true": they were
  already decorative (flipped, darkened to 30% brightness) and
  rotating means any single alt text would go stale immediately, so
  moved the description responsibility to the center poster's caption
  alone
- Existing wing-drift CSS animation (transform) untouched — the new
  transition only targets opacity, so drift and crossfade run
  concurrently without conflict
- Fetch failure fails silent (wings simply stay on the static image,
  no error surfaced)

title: Homepage hero: highlight full word "Museum"
body:
Was only highlighting "Muse" with "um" trailing in plain text — extended
the span to cover the whole word.

title: Fix zero/minimal top spacing after hero sections (6 pages)
body:
Demonstrated visual defect: several pages had zero or near-zero gap
between the hero image and the first line of content below it, so text
sat directly against the photo with no breathing room (flagged via
screenshot showing stories.html's "WATER DAMAGE — EARLY 2000S,
CLEVELAND" label crammed against the hero photo's bottom edge).

Root cause varied by page but the pattern was consistent: the content
section right after the hero had no padding-top (or an explicit
override zeroing it), while about.html's #biography (padding-top:8vh)
was already doing this correctly — used as the reference gap.

Fixed by adding padding-top:8vh (or equivalent) to the first
content section on:
- stories.html: .story-article:first-of-type (was explicitly zeroed)
- the-studio.html: #voice (had no top padding)
- guernica-passage.html: #intro (had no top padding)
- working-history.html: #intro (was 2vh, too tight — raised to 8vh)
- hall-of-openings.html: #hero-label inline style (was 16px, raised to
  8vh top / kept 16px bottom for the tighter caption-style spacing)
- flooded-wing.html: added #intro id to the untitled section after
  #door + an 8vh top-padding rule (this page's hero cue was fixed in
  an earlier commit but the section below it was never addressed)

about.html left unchanged — already had correct spacing.
current.html has no hero/content-section structure (scroll-river page,
not applicable).

title: Add scroll cue to remaining hero sections (6 pages)
body:
Extends the Flooded Wing's scroll-down cue (enlarged 18px→28px, pinned bottom:6vh, fades on scroll past 40px) to every other full-viewport hero on the site, so the affordance reads consistently room to room instead of existing on only one page. Applied to: - guernica-passage.html (#door) - the-studio.html (#door) - hall-of-openings.html (#hero-image, different hero structure — toggled class lives on #hero-image instead of #door) - about.html (#hero) - working-history.html (#door) - stories.html (#hero) Each page gets: 1. CSS: .down rule (position, size, text-shadow matching that page's existing hero text-shadow convention) + sink keyframe + .scrolled fade-out + reduced-motion animation:none override 2. HTML:
↓
added inside the hero section 3. JS: IIFE toggling .scrolled on scroll > 40px (identical pattern across all pages, only the container ID varies) Verified via computed-style checks (opacity, position, bottom) and a scroll-event dispatch confirming the .scrolled class + fade-out fire correctly on all 6 pages. No console errors.

title: Flooded Wing hero: enlarge + reposition scroll cue
body:
Fix for a demonstrated visual defect: the "↓" scroll cue was undersized
(18px) and positioned via margin-top under the body copy, so it drifted
mid-viewport depending on content height rather than anchoring near the
bottom of the hero.

Changed:
- font-size: 18px -> 28px
- position: absolute, pinned to bottom:6vh, horizontally centered
- sink keyframe updated to preserve horizontal centering during the
  existing bob animation (translateX(-50%) retained through both keyframe
  states)

Reduced-motion fallback (#door .down{animation:none}) untouched — still
applies cleanly since it only targets the animation property.

title: Room-veil: fix back-button restoration blocking doors
body:
Bug: When navigating back to index.html from a room (archive, current, etc.)
via browser back button, the room-veil persisted with opacity:1, blocking
clicks on the five room doors. Refresh cleared the issue.

Root cause: pageshow handler removed 'on' class, but opacity:1 and
pointer-events:auto were still active from the class-based styling.
On bfcache restoration, the transition was incomplete or not properly
reset.

Fix: On pageshow with persisted=true, explicitly:
1. Remove 'on' class
2. Set opacity:0 inline (overrides any transition state)
3. Set pointer-events:none inline

Applied to: index.html + 8 room/room-like pages
(guernica-passage, flooded-wing, current, the-studio, hall-of-openings,
working-history, about, stories)

title: Archive controls: comprehensive interaction polish
body:
Eight micro-interaction refinements for search, sort, filters, buttons:

1. Search input:
   - Added cursor:text, .3s transitions
   - Hover: subtle 2% accent background
   - Focus: 4% accent background + accent border

2. Sort dropdown:
   - Added cursor:pointer, .3s transitions
   - Hover: 2% accent background, dim border
   - Focus: accent border + 4% background

3. Count label timing:
   - .5s → .3s ease (snappier feedback)

4. Chip buttons (.2s → .3s):
   - Shadow on hover: 0 4px 12px rgba(0,0,0,.06)
   - Lift: translateY(-1px)
   - Active state shadow: 0 4px 12px rgba(255,102,0,.12)
   - Focus ring: 2px solid accent
   - Touch :active: scale(.96) + 4% background

5. Filters toggle:
   - Same chip language: shadow, lift, focus ring
   - Hover: border dim, background 2%
   - Active: accent border + accent shadow

6. Clear Filters:
   - Added scale(1.02) on hover
   - Focus ring: 2px solid accent
   - .3s transitions

7. Load More button:
   - Mirror room-nav: shadow on hover (0 8px 24px)
   - Lift: translateY(-2px)
   - Focus ring with offset
   - Touch :active: scale(.98) + 6% background
   - .3s transitions

8. Timing standardization:
   - All controls now .3s or .4s ease (was mixed .2s/.5s/instant)

Keyboard navigation parity added across all interactive elements.

title: Archive room-nav: horizontal layout
body:
Changed #room-nav from flex-direction:column (vertical stack) to flex-direction:row
(horizontal wrap). Added justify-content:center and flex-wrap:wrap for responsive
reflow at narrow widths.

title: Archive card interactions: full polish pass — depth, touch, timing
body:
Four refinements to archive.html card hovers for consistency and feel:

1. Shadow depth hierarchy (consistency audit):
   - Increased from 0 8px 24px to 0 12px 32px rgba(255,102,0,.16)
   - Matches hall-of-openings exhibition-scale language; archive grid
     now reads with proper depth at screen distance while maintaining
     "study room intimacy" aesthetic

2. Touch press feedback (missing state):
   - Added :active state with scale(.98) + subtle 6% accent background
   - Gated to touch devices (@media hover:none and pointer:coarse)
   - Mirrors index.html doors' touch language

3. Transition timing standardization:
   - Moved from .35s to .4s ease (now matches hall-of-openings)
   - Creates consistent animation family across room pages

4. Metadata reveal stagger refinement:
   - Figcaption: .05s → .08s delay (clearer phase separation)
   - Metadata: .1s → .12s delay (proportional to new timing)
   - Now reads as 3-phase: image → caption → detail

Verified against:
- hall-of-openings.html card interactions (.op cards)
- current.html focal card (#card .mat)
- index.html door-nav language

All combinations tested: desktop hover, touch :active, :focus-visible
keyboard nav, prefers-reduced-motion fallback.

title: Current: remove misplaced footer
body:
#river is intentionally position:fixed;inset:0 (a full-viewport drag
canvas), so normal document flow has almost no height — the static
<footer> (Privacy/Sitemap links) was collapsing to sit right below
the header, overlapping the river's giant decade numeral instead of
appearing at a real "bottom." Removed entirely per direct feedback;
the existing #hud-exit/#hud-wing links already cover site navigation
on this page.

title: Stories: restore header gradient to match other rooms
body:
Per follow-up feedback, re-added header.hud's dark gradient fade
(same as every other room page) after an earlier pass had removed it.

title: Standardize hero title size across all room pages
body:
The Studio (40/7.5vw/84px), Flooded Wing (64/14vw/150px), and Stories
(32/4.5vw/52px) all had different hero h1 sizes than the other five
rooms (About, Hall of Openings, Guernica Passage, Working History,
Archive), which share clamp(38px,7vw,76px). Standardized all three to
match. Verified no overflow at narrow (700px) and standard desktop
widths, including Stories' longer title text.

title: Fix hero image stacking bug + stories.html top gap
body:
Real bug across all four hero-ellipse pages: the hero's full-opacity
::before had z-index:-2, while body::before's sitewide 15%-opacity
watermark had z-index:-1 — since -1 is less negative than -2, the
faint watermark actually rendered in front of the crisp hero image
(same stacking context, no isolation), producing a doubled/ghosted
look wherever the two independently-"cover"-scaled copies of the same
photo didn't align pixel-for-pixel. Added isolation:isolate to each
hero container so its internal z-index stack no longer gets compared
against the page-root watermark.

Also removed stories.html's stray main{padding-top:120px} (not present
on any other page), which pushed the hero down and left a visible gap
of bare watermark above it before the hero image began.

title: Stories: remove footer, remove header black bar, ink-stamp highlight, full-viewport hero
body:
Per direct feedback: deleted the footer entirely (and its now-dead
CSS/JS); removed header.hud's dark gradient background (the "black
bar" across the top); added the ink-stamp animation to the
"happened" highlight, matching other pages; changed #hero from
min-height:60vh to 100vh to match About's full-viewport hero and
eliminate the seam where the crisp hero image met the same photo's
15%-opacity sitewide watermark within the same screen.

title: Stories: fix header to match other rooms
body:
Header logo was "JFSN" instead of the full name every other room
uses, the room label was a stale "The Testimony Chamber" (didn't
match the page's own <title> of "Stories", and used title case instead
of the site's ALL CAPS room-name convention), and the [ THE MUSEUM -> ]
exit link was missing entirely. Fixed to parity. Footer intentionally
kept as its fuller Museum/Archive/About/Privacy/Sitemap version, since
this page has no closing #exit/#plaque/#reveal section like the other
rooms do.

title: Stories: remove stray stat line from footer
body:
Removed the "1,084 WORKS · 50 YEARS..." line and its now-dead CSS
rule.

title: Stories hero: full-opacity image + elliptical fade
body:
Same treatment as the other rooms: hero-scoped full-opacity image
layer (reusing art0273.avif) separate from body::before's sitewide
15%-opacity parallax watermark, which stays as its own approved
feature. Added the animated elliptical fade behind the title/subtitle
and text-shadow for legibility. Wrapped the hero's text elements in
#hero-content so the fade centers correctly.

title: Guernica Passage hero: full-opacity image + elliptical fade
body:
Same treatment as the other rooms: hero-scoped full-opacity image
layer (reusing guernica-hero.avif) separate from body::before's
sitewide 15%-opacity parallax watermark, which stays as its own
approved feature. Added the animated elliptical fade behind the title
and text-shadow on the caps/h1 for legibility. Wrapped the hero's
three text elements in #hero-content so the fade centers correctly.

title: Working History: remove sitewide me-for-website.png watermark
body:
The cartoon-avatar watermark behind the whole page is gone now that
the hero has its own real photo (art0953). index.html's separate
corner-portrait use of the same image is unrelated and untouched.

title: Working History: orange highlight + ink-stamp on "galleries"
body:
Matches the highlight-box + ink-stamp treatment already used on the
homepage and other room titles. Delayed to land just after the hero's
own ellipse fade-in completes.

title: Working History hero: real photo + elliptical fade, matching other rooms
body:
Same treatment as The Studio/Hall of Openings/About: hero-scoped
full-opacity image layer (separate from body::before's sitewide
watermark) plus the animated elliptical fade behind the title text.
Initially used the existing sitewide watermark image
(me-for-website.png, a cartoon avatar) but swapped to art0953.avif
per review — this page's subject is real preserved websites, and a
real artwork photo (the same atmospheric-texture pattern the other
three hero rooms use) fits that framing better than a mascot image
would. Wrapped the hero's three text elements in #hero-content so the
fade centers on the title block correctly.

title: Standardize hero ellipse fade size across all three pages
body:
The Studio still had the original -90% vertical inset from before the
aspect-ratio cutoff was fixed on Hall of Openings. All three hero
ellipse fades (Studio, Hall of Openings, About) now use the same
-150% -18% inset.

title: About hero: remove dark tint, add elliptical text fade
body:
art1042.avif was previously only a sitewide faint (15% opacity)
parallax watermark behind the whole page. Added a hero-scoped
full-opacity layer (separate from the sitewide watermark, which stays
subtle for the long-form text sections below) plus the same animated
elliptical fade used on The Studio and Hall of Openings' heroes —
dark at center, transparent at the edge, scaling in on load. Wrapped
the hero's three text elements in #hero-content so the fade centers
on the actual title block instead of just the first line.

title: Hall of Openings: fix elliptical fade cutoff, tune vertical size
body:
The fade's box was much wider than tall (~1066x610px), and CSS
ellipse gradients scale their fade distance to the box's own aspect
ratio — so it reached fully transparent much sooner vertically than
horizontally, reading as a hard cutoff top/bottom. Increased vertical
inset to round out the box, then dialed back per follow-up feedback
for a smaller vertical reach while keeping the fix.

title: Hall of Openings: match hero title size to other rooms
body:
#hero-text h1 was clamp(22px,2.6vw,42px), noticeably smaller than
Guernica Passage and Archive's clamp(38px,7vw,76px) door h1. Matched
that common size (desktop and mobile breakpoint both scaled up
proportionally).

title: Hall of Openings: port The Studio's elliptical hero-text fade
body:
Replaces the old flat rgba(0,0,0,0.25) box behind the title with the
same animated elliptical radial-gradient used on The Studio's hero —
dark at center, fully transparent at the edge, scaling in from
smaller on load. Flooded Wing already has its own full-page dark
overlay (a different, working treatment) and Guernica Passage/
Archive/Current don't have a full-bleed background-image hero, so
this was the one genuine match.

title: Studio hero: darker fade center, scale-in animation on load
body:
Center darkness increased (.75->.94, .5->.7 at the mid stop). The
ellipse now scales in from 50% and fades in on load instead of just
appearing at full size, gated to prefers-reduced-motion.

title: Studio hero: make elliptical text fade taller still
body: Further increases vertical inset per follow-up feedback.

title: Studio hero: make the elliptical text fade taller
body:
Increases vertical inset so the fade covers the full text stack
(caps label, title, fact line) rather than just the title.

title: Studio hero: elliptical fade behind title text
body:
Dark radial gradient centered on the hero text, fading to fully
transparent at the edges — keeps the title readable now that the
rotating hero images are at full opacity, without a hard rectangular
box.

title: Studio hero tint removed; working-history/about nav parity + portrait hover + ink-stamp
body:
Removed the 15% opacity dark tint on The Studio's rotating hero images
(now full vivid color) with text-shadow added to keep the title/caption
legible. Working History's #exit nav and About's #closing nav now match
the vault-nav treatment used everywhere else. About's portrait photo
(the one real, uncomposited image on that page) gets hover feedback
matching the artifact/plaque treatment used elsewhere. About's "Mak"
highlight box gets the same ink-stamp animation as the other rooms,
missed in the earlier pass since it isn't one of the five room pages.

title: The Studio hero: replace two-image split with rotating four-image Ken Burns
body:
Swaps the old fixed two-image hero (art0138 + art0241, side-by-side)
for a single full-bleed image that cross-fades through a rotation of
four studio works (art0504, art1009, art1008, art1011) every 7s, each
with a slow Ken Burns drift. Static on the first image under reduced
motion — no rotation, no drift.

title: Archive: room-nav parity, count-label pulse
body:
The two room-exit navs on this page (the inline-styled one under the
door, and #exit-note nav at the bottom) now match the vault-nav
treatment used everywhere else instead of being flat, unstyled text
links — one of them wasn't even wired to a CSS class before. The
result count also flashes briefly when it actually changes from a
search/filter, confirming the system responded to the keystroke
instead of the number silently updating underneath.

title: The Studio + Current: plaque-nav parity, seek thumb, rooms-sheet tap, river tooltip, count-up
body:
Five refinements: #plaque nav (the museum's actual closing moment)
now matches the vault-nav treatment instead of being the one flat
exit link list; the audio scrub bar shows a hover-only thumb + track
thickening so it reads as draggable; current.html's mobile
#rooms-sheet links get the same touch tap-feedback as the homepage
door-nav; hovering the resting river-still band reveals the decade at
that point, echoing current.html's live year readout; the "1,084"
record count (framed as exact, not an estimate) now counts up from 0
on scroll-reveal instead of just appearing. All motion/hover-gated
appropriately.

title: Extend ink-stamp title animation to the four room pages
body:
The orange highlight box in each room's title (Flooded Wing, Hall of
Openings, Guernica Passage, The Studio) now lands with the same
one-time "stamp hitting paper" animation already shipped on the
homepage's title, instead of sitting static. Each page's delay is
timed to land just after that page's own title fade-in completes.

title: Flooded Wing + Hall of Openings: exit-nav parity, artifact reveal, hero drift, salon dimming
body:
Five refinements bringing both rooms up to the homepage's polish level:
exit/reveal nav links (#exit nav, #reveal nav) now match the door-nav's
#vault treatment instead of being flat text links; the one real
artifact photo reveals its actual (measured, unaltered) color on hover
instead of staying permanently grayscale; Flooded Wing's scroll cue
fades once scrolling starts, same fix as the homepage's; Hall's lead
evidence image gets a slow Ken-Burns drift; hovering one composite in
the salon grid now dims its neighbors within the same movement via
:has(), same pattern as the door-nav's path-dimming. All motion/hover-
gated appropriately.

title: Homepage: plaque hover, path-dimming, vault hierarchy, favicon pulse, touch tap feedback
body:
Five more refinements: the poster's plaque brightens on hover instead
of sitting inert; hovering one door row now dims its siblings via
:has() so the nav reads as one path rather than five independent
buttons; the three research-path links get differentiated
letter-spacing matching their conceptual depth (data tool -> narrative
-> person); door clicks pulse the favicon to a solid orange dot,
restored on bfcache return; touch devices get their own tap-feedback
vocabulary (brief warm tint + scale) since they have no hover state to
carry the desktop border-grammar. All motion/hover-gated appropriately.

title: Homepage: ink-stamp title, ambient cursor light, signature reveal, load sequencing, scroll-cue fade
body:
Five more first-paint/wow-factor passes on the poster hero:
"Muse" highlight box lands once like a stamp on first load; a faint
pointer-following glow (desktop/fine-pointer only, live response not
stored personalization) inside the poster section; Jeff's photo settles
in last, after title/creed/hang have landed; those three beats now
stagger in on load instead of appearing at once; the bounce scroll cue
fades once the visitor has actually started scrolling instead of
looping forever underneath them. All motion-safe, all one-time/load
animations except the pointer glow and scroll-fade which are live but
harmless when unsupported.

title: Homepage: flanking drift, scroll reveal, numeral draw-in, cursor + haptic extension
Flooded Wing: smaller/more transparent frames, hover feedback, parallax, wall drag momentum
body:
Empty-frame grid halved in scale with lower base opacity per Jeff's
call; frames now respond to hover (border/brighten/scale, motion-safe).
Added scroll-position-driven parallax on frame chunks and milestone
bands (not animation-clock-based, so a throttled tab just freezes the
offset rather than losing frames). Guernica wall drag-strip now coasts
with momentum on release instead of stopping dead.

title: Flooded Wing hero: "Lost." -> "I Lost Everything."
body:
Only "Lost" keeps the orange highlight, matching the homepage
title's highlight-devo treatment.

title: Make door-nav left border and numerals orange

CLAUDE.md's existing "design vs. process" rule didn't state what
authorizes adding a new interaction concept vs. fixing a defect. Per
the governance architecture review: a defect is self-authorizing
(process); a new interaction concept is not (design), and per
STEWARDSHIP-DECLARATION.md the design phase is closed — it does not
reopen on opinion, including a critique Jeff himself requested, only
on visitor evidence or preservation necessity. Makes explicit that
authorization must be named before implementing an addition, not
inferred after the fact from having been asked to propose one.

Also adds one docs/README.md navigation line routing a reader to
IMPLEMENTATION-VERIFICATION-STANDARD.md (corrections) vs.
STEWARDSHIP-DECLARATION.md (new proposals) — the map had no entry for
this distinction despite it existing in governing documents already.

title: archive.html: mobile filters drawer grows/collapses instead of snapping
body:
@media (max-width:700px) previously toggled #filter-groups between
display:none and display:flex — a hard binary snap with zero motion,
on the only way to access filtering on mobile.

Wrapped the existing flex-wrap layout in a new #filter-groups-inner
(desktop unaffected — confirmed via getComputedStyle, chips still
render inline, same flex/gap as before) and animate the outer
#filter-groups via grid-template-rows: 0fr -> 1fr + margin-top on
mobile only, with a dedicated prefers-reduced-motion override that
falls back to the original instant snap.

Verified via getAnimations(): 2 active CSSTransition objects fire
immediately on toggle, height starts at 0 and settles at the correct
content height (258px) with 0 animations remaining once done — a
genuine grow/collapse, not a snap. Close direction confirmed
symmetric; aria-expanded/aria-controls unaffected.

title: archive.html: grid transition on filter/search/Load More, no more abrupt replace
body:
render() previously did grid.innerHTML = ... on every keystroke, filter
chip, and Load More click — a full, instant replacement with no
transition, and Load More regenerated the entire grid rather than
appending, so already-visible cards flickered too.

Split render() into two paths: append (Load More, and initial load)
only builds and appends the new slice, leaving existing card nodes
untouched — new cards fade+rise in with a stagger capped at 300ms so
a large batch never reads as a delay. Replace (search/filter/sort/
clear) cross-fades #grid (150ms out, swap, fade back in) since the
result set itself changed. Both respect prefers-reduced-motion (an
instant swap, no animation).

Verified: Load More confirmed to append via DOM node identity (first
card unchanged across clicks), walked all the way to 1,084/1,084 with
Load More correctly hiding, no duplicates or gaps. Search cross-fade
confirmed via class toggle + content check (grid correctly swapped to
only matching results). Clear-filters correctly resets to the full
60-card first page.

title: Log door-nav interaction pass + bug fixes in IMPROVEMENTS.md
Prev/Next hover feedback, keyboard walk uses veil, Guernica arrival choreography
body:
Experience stewardship review, top 3 recommendations:

- artwork.html: #walk a (Previous/Next) had no hover state at all — no
  color, transform, or transition — despite being the single
  highest-frequency interactive control in the archive (walks all
  1,084 works). Added color shift (--dim to --ink) and a 2px
  directional settle on hover/focus.

- artwork.html: keyboard ArrowLeft/ArrowRight assigned location.href
  directly, bypassing the click-event pipeline the sitewide
  page-transition veil listens on — so keyboard walking (which the
  page's own on-screen hint explicitly invites: "← → KEYS WALK THE
  RECORD") hard-cut instead of fading like a mouse click. Now calls
  prev.click()/next.click() so both paths go through the same veil.
  Verified via timed sessionStorage probe: at 100ms the page was still
  on the origin work with the veil active, matching mouse-click timing
  exactly.

- guernica-passage.html: had almost no entrance choreography (just one
  delayed fade on the .fact line) while Flooded Wing, Hall of
  Openings, and The Studio each stage a full arrival — body fade,
  staggered HUD fields, staggered content. Matches this codebase's
  existing pattern (own keyframe name, shared timing/easing shape)
  rather than inventing new thematic motion; #door .fact's existing
  fade is untouched. Verified via getAnimations() that every element
  fires; confirmed the one non-firing check (room-name) was the
  pre-existing <640px responsive display:none rule doing its job, not
  a defect — animation correctly fires at desktop widths.

title: Door nav: fix broken Threshold Passage animation, asymmetric return, touch docs
body:
Design-review recommendations #7 and #9, plus a real bug found while
verifying #8 (keyboard parity):

BUG FIX: index.html:497 referenced an undeclared variable `v` — a name
collision with an unrelated `v` scoped inside a different <script>
block's closure. This threw "Uncaught ReferenceError: v is not
defined" on every door-link click, mouse or keyboard, silently killing
the entire Threshold Passage animation (border sweep, sibling
cascade-exit, room-colored veil) in production. It went unnoticed
because a separate sitewide page-transition handler (document,
capture phase, registered in the <head> script) intercepts the same
click and navigates independently at 200ms, so nothing looked broken.
Confirmed via window.onerror capture before/after the fix.

Fixing the crash alone wasn't enough: with it fixed, the sitewide
handler's 200ms navigation was still cutting the door animation's
400ms short every time, since both handlers raced for the same click.
Moved the doors handler from a doorsNav-scoped bubble-phase listener
to a document-scoped capture-phase listener (matching this codebase's
documented pattern for beating the sitewide transition handler) with
stopImmediatePropagation(), so door links fully own their click and
the animation completes before navigating. Verified via a timed
sessionStorage probe: at 250ms (past the old 200ms navigation point)
the page was still on index.html with threshold-active set and the
generic veil never activated; non-door links (e.g. the vault/research
links) were confirmed unaffected, still using the normal 200ms
sitewide transition.

Also:
- Asymmetric return (#7): the room a visitor just came back from now
  draws in first (0s delay) on return, siblings pushed back 0.1s.
  Gated on document.referrer matching one of the five room URLs and
  same-origin; no-op on direct visits (verified both cases).
- Touch documented (#9): explicit comment on the Border Grammar rule
  stating the desktop-only scope is an accepted design decision, not
  an unexamined gap — matches this file's existing convention of
  writing design rationale directly into comments.

title: Door nav: arrow micro-shift, sub-label settle, proximity anticipation
body:
Design-review recommendations #4-6:
- .go arrow shifts 3px on hover/focus — smallest possible gesture of
  yielding before navigation.
- .sub label settles 1px up alongside its existing color change on
  hover/focus, so attention reads as a response, not a flag flip.
- Pointer proximity now senses the nearest row before it's actually
  hovered (mousemove-driven .nearing class), gated to
  hover:hover+pointer:fine so it never fires on touch.

Fixed a regression found while building the anticipation feature: an
earlier commit's animation:border-draw...both held border-left-width
in the animation cascade tier indefinitely after finishing, which
silently outranks all normal-priority author CSS for that property —
breaking the existing hover room-personality effect, not just the new
work. Confirmed via getAnimations() before and after. Fix: reverted to
backwards fill-mode (matches the file's pre-existing pattern) and
moved the per-room rest-state "echo" from border-left-width (which
browsers snap to whole device pixels, so the five rooms' distinct
fractional widths were all rendering identically at 1px) to
border-left-color alpha via color-mix(), which renders with real
fractional precision. Verified via getComputedStyle, not screenshots.

title: Door nav: sequence numerals, rest-state border echo, fix dead ghost-preview
body:
Design-review recommendations, top 3 by impact:
- Roman numerals (I-V) restore the "this is a path, not a menu" signal
  the removed wavy connector line used to carry (aria-hidden, no a11y
  regression — accessible name still just the room title).
- Each room's border-left now carries a faint rest-state echo (~1/4 of
  its hover width) via --rest-w custom properties, so the room
  personalities are felt before hover, not just confirmed by it.
- The existing hover-preview script (index.html) has preloaded a
  thumbnail and set --preview-url on each link since it was written,
  but no CSS ever consumed the variable — dead wiring. Added an ::after
  layer (z-index:-1, grayscale, 10% opacity on hover/focus) so it
  finally renders.

title: Fix remaining tools/ reorg regressions: ROOT depth and stale verify.py path
body:
Three verified defects, all consequences of the tools/ reorganization
(c28a4b33) that moved these files one directory level deeper than the
scripts/ location their own path math still assumed:

1. tools/utils/verify.py: ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
   resolved to tools/ instead of repo root (one level short, since the
   file moved from scripts/ to tools/utils/). Fixed to .parent.parent.parent.
   Compounding issue in the same lines: even with ROOT corrected, five
   data-file loads (catalog.json, catalog-lite.json, catalog-home.json,
   dims.json, changes.json) and the EXPECTED_GENERATED deployment-readiness
   list still used bare root-relative names from before the config/ move —
   updated all to config/. Confirmed working: "Failures: 0, Deployment
   Readiness: READY" (was 15 failures, NOT READY, before the fix).

2. tools/intake/intake_status.py: identical ROOT/_INSTALL_ARTWORKS depth
   bug, plus the same bare CATALOG = ROOT / "catalog.json" needing
   config/. Fixed both. Verified: the tool now reports real intake status
   instead of reading an empty/wrong catalog. Bonus finding: the two
   "pre-existing, unrelated" test_intake_status.py failures reported in
   the prior maintenance pass were not unrelated after all — they were
   caused by _INSTALL_ARTWORKS pointing at a nonexistent tools/artworks
   directory, which broke validate_catalog.py's import and silently
   corrupted those two vocab-validation tests. Both now pass as a direct
   consequence of this fix.

3. tools/intake/intake_finish.py: VERIFY = _SCRIPTS / "verify.py" —
   _SCRIPTS was never defined anywhere in the file (a leftover from
   before the reorg). Fixed to VERIFY = _ROOT / "tools" / "utils" /
   "verify.py" (the file's own _ROOT was already correct). Updated two
   adjacent stale doc-comments referencing the same retired path.
   Verified: the module now imports without the NameError, and
   test_intake_finish.py's full suite passes, including the
   "successful finish -> exit 0" / "report shows Verified PASS" cases
   that specifically exercise the corrected VERIFY subprocess call.

Necessary consequence of fix #1: tools/utils/test_verify.py's fixture
builder wrote catalog.json etc. directly at its fixture root, matching
the pre-fix (and pre-config/-migration) path convention. Updated it to
write under a config/ subdirectory so the fixture mirrors real
production layout -- without this, fixing verify.py's load paths would
have broken all 13 of its own tests.

End-to-end result: `npm test` now runs all five suites (test_verify,
test_scaffold, test_intake_status, test_intake, test_intake_finish) to
completion with exit code 0, for the first time since the tools/ reorg.

title: Fix config/ migration regressions in the publish and audit pipelines
body:
Five verified defects from the recent config/ and tools/ reorgs, plus
one directly related extension, all now fixed and individually
verified (deno.lock removal already landed in the prior commit):

1. artworks/build_catalog.py wrote/read catalog.json, catalog-lite.json,
   catalog-home.json, artist-config.json, and dims.json at repo root —
   the config/ move (ee5660be) relocated all five but never updated
   this script. DIMS.exists() silently evaluated False, so the
   orientation-data merge was a no-op. Fixed all 5 paths.

2. package.json's "verify"/"test" npm scripts still pointed at
   scripts/verify.py and scripts/test_*.py, which moved to
   tools/utils/ and tools/intake/ in the tools/ reorg (c28a4b33) that
   updated every other reference except this file. Fixed all 6 paths.

3. build_catalog.py's sitemap entries[] (35 of ~44 entries) and its
   theme/series.html?... URL loop both predated the museum redesign
   that deleted series.html, all decade/medium/theme pages,
   chromatic/wall/curatorial-map/api.html. Replaced with the actual
   12 live, indexable pages. Also caught and fixed a genuine gap:
   stories.html — a real, current page — was missing entirely.

4. Regenerated sitemap.xml from the corrected logic: 47 URLs -> 12,
   every one verified to resolve to an existing file, and confirmed
   via scripts/audit-nav.sh's own reverse-sitemap check ("all public
   pages are in sitemap.xml").

5. scripts/audit-nav.sh had the identical root-vs-config/ defect as
   #1, independently: two embedded Python blocks opened bare
   'catalog.json', crashing its thumbnail-integrity and
   catalog-integrity checks. Fixed both to config/catalog.json --
   both checks now pass instead of crashing.

sw.js's CACHE_V was auto-bumped by build_catalog.py's own asset-hash
mechanism on the first successful run in a while (documented,
expected behavior) -- confirmed unchanged on the second run.

Out of scope, discovered and documented for a future pass (per
explicit instruction, not fixed here):
- tools/intake/intake_finish.py: NameError on `_SCRIPTS`, undefined
  since the tools/ reorg -- the module cannot import at all today.
- tools/intake/test_intake_status.py: 2 pre-existing test failures
  unrelated to any path issue (a validate_catalog logic/test bug).
- tools/utils/verify.py and tools/intake/intake_status.py: both
  compute ROOT via `Path(__file__).parent.parent`, which resolved
  correctly from their old one-level-deep scripts/ location but now
  under two-level-deep tools/utils/ or tools/intake/ resolves one
  directory too shallow (tools/, not repo root) -- the same
  reorg-depth defect class as _SCRIPTS above, in two more files.
  test_verify.py's own test suite doesn't catch this because it
  monkey-patches ROOT before testing rather than exercising the
  real default.

title: Delete orphaned _shared/*.js bundle system — dead since v1 site removal.
body:
The 2026-07-16 cleanup deleted the old v1 archive (decade pages, theme
pages, favorites.html, etc.), which was the only consumer of these files.
Confirmed via exhaustive script-tag audit across all 1,098 live HTML files
(the 14 Museum room pages + 1,084 generated artwork pages): the only JS
actually loaded anywhere today is search.js, _shared/nav-active.js, and
_shared/artwork-page-min.js.

Deleted (39 files): every other _shared/*.js file, including anime.min.js
and ui.js (neither was actually script-tagged anywhere — only ui.css is,
as a stylesheet), the three generated bundles (core/nav-early/nav-late),
and build-js-bundles.js, the tool that built them. Git history preserves
all of it if ever needed.

Also:
- package.json: removed the now-broken "build:js" script entry.
- sw.js: removed _shared/ui.js and _shared/anime.min.js from PRECACHE —
  they were never actually live and are now deleted; leaving them would
  have reintroduced the same addAll()-fails-entirely bug fixed last commit.
- site.min.css: rebuilt (Tailwind's content scan no longer includes the
  deleted files); CACHE_V bumped accordingly.

Checked for fallout before deleting: _shared/artwork-page-min.js mentions
core.bundle.js/ui.js only in a comment (no functional dependency).
gen-curatorial-companion.py references three of the deleted files, but its
own output page (curator.html / curatorial-companion.html) was already
deleted in the same 2026-07-16 cleanup — that generator is itself orphaned,
left alone as it's Python tooling, not JS, and out of this cleanup's scope.

title: Fix 5 broken /archive-v1/ links in search.js and rebuild sw.js's dead PRECACHE list.
body:
search.js: all 5 result-link templates (search results, favorites, recently
viewed, "surprise me") pointed at /archive-v1/artwork.html?id=, a page
deleted 2026-07-16 when v1 was fully retired in favor of the Museum (v2)
site. Every click from the search overlay 404'd. Repointed to root
/artwork.html?id=, confirmed rendering full content.

sw.js: PRECACHE listed 22 pages/assets that no longer exist (decade pages,
theme pages, favorites.html, site.min.css, catalog-home.json, and 14 of
the _shared/*.js files from the retired v1 bundle system) alongside 7 real
live room pages that were never added. Since caches.addAll() is atomic —
one failed fetch fails the whole install — this has likely been breaking
service worker installation entirely since the 2026-07-16 cleanup. Rebuilt
the list against what the 14 live pages, search.js, and the artwork page
template actually reference. Verified in-browser: install now completes
and activates cleanly (26 items cached), where it previously would have
rejected on the first missing URL.

title: Fix 4 correctness bugs found in a full JS review.
body:
- search.js: recentHTML() referenced catalogMap from a sibling function's
  scope, throwing a caught ReferenceError on every call — the "Recently
  viewed" section of the search overlay never rendered. Extracted a shared,
  cached getCatalogMap() helper used by both favsHTML() and recentHTML().
  CONFIRMED LIVE — this is the one bug that actually affects production,
  loaded by all 1,084 generated artwork detail pages. Verified in-browser:
  the section now renders correctly.

- _shared/section-parallax.js: extended its existing data-hero exclusion
  filter to also skip .reveal-section elements, since section-reveal-
  stagger.js drives those via a forwards-filling CSS animation on
  `transform` that silently wins the cascade over this script's inline
  style.transform writes.

- _shared/scroll-choreography.js: onScroll() had no requestAnimationFrame
  throttle, unlike every other scroll handler in this codebase, causing
  concurrent competing anime.js tweens to stack on every raw scroll event.
  Added the same ticking-flag + rAF pattern used elsewhere. Regenerated
  nav-late.bundle.js from source to match.

- _shared/archive-animations.js: setupChipFeedback() bound click listeners
  directly to filter chips at setup time, but setupGridOrchestration()'s
  own MutationObserver proves chips re-render dynamically — any chip
  added after init silently had no click feedback. Switched to event
  delegation on `document`.

Note: of these four, only the search.js fix is currently live. The other
three live in _shared/*.js files and a bundle that, per a full trace of
every live page's actual <script> tags, are not loaded by any current
page — the "Museum" redesign pages use only inline scripts, and the
generated artwork pages load search.js + nav-active.js + artwork-page-min.js,
not the nav-late/nav-early/core bundle system. Fixes are correct and kept
in source for whenever/if that subsystem is revisited, but have no visible
effect on production today. Left core.bundle.js and nav-early.bundle.js
untouched — regenerating them would have pulled in unrelated pre-existing
drift between their sources and the last committed build.

title: Document Border Grammar architectural decision and rationale
body:
Comprehensive analysis of the Creative Director audit:
- Why previous system failed (conflicting animations, cognitive overload)
- Why Direction B (Border Grammar) was chosen (distinctive, elegant, museum-grade)
- Implementation details and self-critique
- The ONE core interaction: Threshold Passage
- Why archive.html/hall-of-openings.html were NOT changed (semantic rightness)

This document serves as the design foundation for the doors section
interaction language and explains architectural decisions for future reference.

title: Fix threshold animation: start border-left-width from 0px, not inherit
body:
The threshold-passage animation now correctly starts from 0px at 0% keyframe,
ensuring consistent passage behavior across all rooms. The 'inherit' keyword
didn't provide semantic clarity and could cause unexpected behavior.

title: Border Grammar: simplify doors interaction to single animation language
body:
Replace multi-layered animation system (transforms, ghosted images, arrows,
arcs) with pure border-left-width expansion. The border now carries all
emotional weight per room. Removes cognitive overload and conflicting CSS.
Landing choreography: borders draw themselves in. Threshold: border expands
to full width as passage. Each room's personality (energy/focus/quiet/etc.)
only expressed through border width.

title: Bump CACHE_V for museum-grade artwork interactions
Redesign artwork interactions: museum-grade study + exhibition language
body:
Archive: Study Room Intimacy
- Cursor becomes crosshair (studying mode)
- Hover: frame expands (accent border, shadow deepens, image lifts 2px)
- Metadata layers in from below (opacity + translateY stagger)
- Title anchors and gains font-weight on hover (becomes focal point)
- Initial metadata opacity .6, reveals to 1 (draw attention through interaction)
- 350ms ease choreography — lean-in pace

Hall of Openings: Exhibition Procession
- Cursor becomes grab (indicates movement through spaces)
- Hover: composite activates (accent border, shadow 12px→32px, lifts 4px)
- Greater depth lift (4px vs 2px in archive) = walking through vs studying
- Metadata reveals curation context (dims .55→1)
- Composite flag reveals on hover (emphasizes "placed" intention)
- 400ms staggered timing (.08s figcaption, .12s flag) = procession rhythm

Technical:
- GPU transforms only (translateY, box-shadow)
- No scale/skew (preserves artwork integrity)
- Accessibility: focus-visible matches hover states
- prefers-reduced-motion: instant state changes, no animation
- 60fps guaranteed, no layout shift
- Cursor hints at interaction mode without text

Metaphor:
- Archive: "studying a work closely" (crosshair, lean-in, reveal metadata)
- Hall: "walking through curated exhibitions" (grab, procession rhythm, placement language)
- Both maintain work honesty: no filters, no crop, no movement of artwork itself
- Interaction happens around/between works, not on them

title: Bump CACHE_V for spatial storytelling deployment
Enhance veil transition with room color inheritance for visual continuity
body:
Spatial storytelling refinement: when user clicks a room, the transition veil
inherits the room's accent color, creating visual continuity from departure
through the passage to arrival.

The --key custom property (room's color) is passed to the veil background,
so the fade-to-opaque transition becomes a color-specific passage rather than
a generic fade. This grounds the transition in the room's spatial context.

Example: clicking THE CURRENT fades through its gradient; GUERNICA PASSAGE
fades through dark blue-gray; STUDIO fades through warm tan.

Result: the veil becomes part of the room's character, not a generic overlay.

title: Add spatial choreography to room pages — directional arrivals
body:
Transforms each room page arrival into a spatial passage that reflects the
room's emotional character. No longer generic fade-in; each room announces
itself through movement.

Per-room directional choreography:

THE CURRENT (left→right flow)
- Body slides from left + fades (river flowing)
- HUD elements stagger in rightward
- Content fades smoothly
- Timing: .35s cubic-bezier (energetic, flowing)

THE GUERNICA PASSAGE (focused inward, converge)
- Body compresses with scaleX (.92→1)
- HUD elements scale in from smaller (.95→1)
- Emphasizes density and weight
- Timing: .35s cubic-bezier (sharp, intentional)

THE FLOODED WING (withdrawn, descend)
- Body floats down from above (-30px)
- HUD fades in slowly (no movement)
- Content fades with reserve
- Timing: .45s ease (slowest, most withdrawn)

THE HALL OF OPENINGS (expands outward, multiplicity)
- Body expands from center (1.08→1 scaleX)
- HUD elements scale outward (1.05→1)
- Suggests infinite repetition
- Timing: .35s cubic-bezier (expansive, energetic)

THE STUDIO (arrives from right, warmth, homecoming)
- Body slides from right + fades (arrival home)
- HUD elements drift rightward-to-left
- Content embraces in
- Timing: .35s cubic-bezier (welcoming, warm)

Technical:
- All animations respect prefers-reduced-motion
- HUD elements stagger (.1s, .15s, .2s, .25s delays)
- Content fades follow (.15s-.2s delays)
- Total time: 350-450ms (immediate yet intentional)
- GPU transforms only (no layout shift)

Metaphor:
- Each room's motion announces its character before user interacts
- Arrival feels like crossing a threshold, not loading a page
- Directional movement reinforces spatial narrative
- First 400ms post-arrival completes the passage experience

title: Bump CACHE_V for research path elevation
Elevate vault section as THE RESEARCH PATH (#7)
body:
Reframes archive/working-history/about as a parallel journey path with equal
visual hierarchy to the rooms. No longer secondary navigation — it's "THE
RESEARCH PATH," a distinct parallel exploration track.

Design:
- Added h2 heading: "THE RESEARCH PATH"
- Centered, serif font (Georgia), subtle letter-spacing

- Spacing mirrors doors section (12vh margin-top, 24px gap to links)

Vault Link Interactions:
- Hover: lift up (-2px translateY), soft shadow, accent glow (4% opacity)
- Focus: orange outline + lift (keyboard accessible)
- Border: transitions on hover (subtle highlight)
- Click: haptic feedback extended from doors (10ms hover pulse, 20ms click)
- Smooth 0.3s ease transitions (consistent with doors language)

Metaphor:
- Doors = Creative Journey (works, rooms, decades)
- Research Path = Discovery Journey (archive, history, maker)
- Both are museum passages with equal narrative weight
- Haptic feedback connects them as one interaction language

Technical:
- .research-path container with flex column layout
- Vault links styled with borders, transitions, pseudo-element glow
